$comment: Parity policy for the shared VfTable cases. Plain data: no DSL, no waiver engine. The table owns no interaction, no id and ships no browser controller; approvedDivergences is empty and no dimension below may be approved for it.

classifications.exact: Must match literally across every target. Structure, canonical classes, native attributes, visible text, accessible names, computed geometry and colour.
classifications.semantic: Framework mechanics may differ; the observable meaning must not. How content is composed, how a renderer marks its own output.
classifications.framework-specific: Historical behaviour of one adapter that the other is not required to reproduce. Narrow, named, and covered by its own test.

notCompared.$comment: Recorded so a reviewer can see what is deliberately outside the comparison, without leaving dead dimensions that look like live protection. Nothing here is a waiver: the extractor never produces these differences in the first place.
notCompared.attributeOrder: Attributes are extracted into a sorted map, so serialisation order cannot produce a difference.
notCompared.classOrder: Canonical classes are extracted as a sorted list. Where a consumer class lands relative to the canonical ones is pinned by the characterization suite and by the Razor component tests, not here.
notCompared.rendererMarkers: Vue scope attributes (data-v-*) and the Razor ownership marker (data-vf-razor*) are dropped by scripts/parity/extract.mjs. Neither adapter writes one for this component.
notCompared.generatedIdLiterals: Generated ids differ between adapters by construction (v-n against r-n); the extractor rewrites every id to its document position and every reference through the same map, so the relationship graph is compared and the literal is not.
notCompared.stickyScroll: No case scrolls. The sticky header is the vf-table--sticky-header class plus a stylesheet rule; the class is compared as DOM, the rule reaches both targets from the same canonical stylesheet, and the scroll container's computed overflow and box are compared as geometry in a height-limited case.

outsideTheCatalog.$comment: Behaviour that is part of the contract and deliberately not represented as a parity case, each with where it is covered instead.
outsideTheCatalog.templateDefaultSlot: A Razor template invocation with any content declares the default slot, even when the content is only named slots, so a template cannot express a header with no body (plan section У.8). The fixture hands slots over through the PHP API, where absence is explicit; the engine behaviour is executed by TableComponentTest.
outsideTheCatalog.slotsAfterMount: The Vue sections follow the slots a parent passes on every render. A server render has no after-mount; pinned by the characterization suite and the mutation table-sections-cached.
outsideTheCatalog.consumerClassOrder: A consumer class is appended after vf-table-wrap. Class order is not a parity dimension (notCompared.classOrder); pinned by the characterization suite and TableComponentTest.

dom.structure.description: An unexpected element, a wrapper or a tag mismatch: the wrapper or the scroll container dropped, the wrapper as a section, the caption outside the table, a row group missing, extra, reordered or rendered as another row group. Never approvable; comparison continues through tag differences so attribute diagnostics remain visible.

dom.canonicalClasses.description: vf-table-wrap and consumer classes on the wrapper, vf-table-scroll, vf-table and its four modifiers on the table, and the caption and row group classes. A modifier on the wrapper, or a consumer class on the table, is a difference here.

dom.nativeAttributes.description: class, style, id, tabindex and any native attribute a consumer forwards - on the wrapper only. The scroll container and the table carry their class and nothing else.

dom.text.description: Visible text content of every element.

dom.aria.description: aria-* attributes and role. The table writes none of its own; a consumer role and aria-label land on the wrapper, never on the table.

dom.productData.description: data-* attributes that belong to the product rather than to a renderer.

dom.relationships.description: A consumer aria-describedby on the wrapper, resolved to the hint it names. The table generates no id, so there is nothing of its own to cross-wire.

style.geometry.description: Computed box metrics of every measured role.

style.colour.description: Computed colour, background and border colour of every measured role.

visual.description: Rendered screenshot of the case, per theme.

a11y.role.description: The role each measured node exposes: the table, its caption and row groups as Chrome exposes them, and a consumer role on the wrapper.

a11y.name.description: The accessible name: the table named by its caption, and the wrapper by a consumer aria-label.

a11y.states.description: Accessibility states exposed by each measured node, including the disabled state Chrome derives for controls inside a disabled fieldset.

static.noInteraction.description: The recorded fact that the component declares no interaction to drive, and that the harness measured this rather than skipping the stage. Consumer-provided controls are counted against the number each case declares; the component-owned count is required to be zero.

historicalQuirks.description: inheritAttrs is false and the attributes are bound onto div.vf-table-wrap, so a consumer aria-label names a div and the table keeps only its class list.
historicalQuirks.reason: Moving them to the table would be the charitable reading and changes what every stylesheet and test selects.

historicalQuirks.description: thead, tbody and tfoot open for the presence of their slot, not for what it renders, so an empty slot is an empty row group.
historicalQuirks.reason: Keying them on content is the obvious tidy-up and a different DOM.

historicalQuirks.description: The caption opens for a truthy prop or a caption slot; the slot replaces the prop and, when it renders nothing, shows the prop text.
historicalQuirks.reason: Letting the prop win, or dropping the fallback, are both plausible ports.

historicalQuirks.description: column-dividers, compact, striped, sticky-header, on the table, whatever order the props are written in.
historicalQuirks.reason: The class set is compared here; the order is pinned by the characterization suite and the shared vectors.
